1	# Stability and analysis options in Pynite
2	
3	This is a lightly formatted copy of the official Pynite manual at the
4	pre-fix source revision.  It is included as public scientific evidence, not as
5	an implementation hint.  Source: <https://github.com/JWock82/Pynite/blob/147c7aa24ec30b1c6a4d4820446915380752877b/docs/source/stability.rst>
6	and <https://github.com/JWock82/Pynite/blob/147c7aa24ec30b1c6a4d4820446915380752877b/docs/source/analysis.rst>.
7	
8	In a three-dimensional model, an object can translate in X, Y, or Z and rotate
9	about X, Y, or Z.  These three translations and three rotations are six
10	degrees of freedom, and all six must be stabilized for an object to be stable.
11	Rigid-body motion occurs when the entire structure can move as a unit because
12	supports are insufficient.  Localized nodal instabilities can remain after the
13	global structure is supported; hinged-ended members meeting at a node are one
14	example described by the manual.  Both situations appear as a singular,
15	unsolvable stiffness system.
16	
17	Pynite exposes a `check_stability=True` option on analysis methods to help
18	isolate these cases.  The manual also notes that the option costs extra
19	analysis time and is normally enabled while debugging a model.
20	
21	The analysis guide documents sparse and dense matrix solvers.  Sparse storage
22	keeps non-zero entries and is the default when SciPy is available; dense mode
23	stores all entries and can be useful for small models.  General analysis is
24	available through `FEModel3D.analyze()`, while `analyze_linear()` assembles a
25	linear model once and superposes load combinations.  These paths are both
26	used by the public workbench.
27	
28	Pynite's manual further distinguishes second-order P-Delta effects from the
29	first-order stability questions exercised here.  The workbench uses static
30	first-order cases so that the observations can be repeated without plotting,
31	network access, or external data.
32

10	def _model_from_case(case: dict, fixture: dict):
11	    # Import through the task's source path so the workbench is self-contained.
12	    from Pynite import FEModel3D
13	
14	    model = FEModel3D()
15	    material = fixture["material"]
16	    section = fixture["section"]
17	    model.add_material(
18	        material["name"], material["E"], material["G"], material["nu"], material["rho"]
19	    )
20	    model.add_section(
21	        section["name"], section["A"], section["Iy"], section["Iz"], section["J"]
22	    )
23	    for name, x, y, z in case["nodes"]:
24	        model.add_node(name, x, y, z)
25	    for name, i, j in case["members"]:
26	        model.add_member(name, i, j, material["name"], section["name"])
27	
28	    for node in case.get("fixed_nodes", []):
29	        model.def_support(node, True, True, True, True, True, True)
30	    for node in case.get("pinned_nodes", []):
31	        # The end supports leave model-axis rotation free, as in a pin/roller
32	        # idealization; the member continuity supplies the remaining restraint.
33	        model.def_support(node, True, True, True, True, True, False)
34	
35	    load = case["load"]
36	    if len(load) == 3:
37	        model.add_node_load(load[0], load[1], load[2])
38	    else:
39	        model.add_member_dist_load(load[0], load[1], load[2], load[3])
40	    if case.get("release"):
41	        member, release = case["release"]
42	        model.def_releases(member, **{release: True})
43	    return model
44	
45	
46	def _scalar(value) -> float:
47	    arr = np.asarray(value, dtype=float)
48	    return float(arr.reshape(-1)[0])
49	
50	
51	def _observe(model) -> dict[str, object]:
52	    displacements: list[float] = []
53	    reactions: list[float] = []
54	    for node in model.nodes.values():
55	        for field in (node.DX, node.DY, node.DZ, node.RX, node.RY, node.RZ):
56	            if "Combo 1" in field:
57	                displacements.append(_scalar(field["Combo 1"]))
58	        for field in (node.RxnFX, node.RxnFY, node.RxnFZ, node.RxnMX, node.RxnMY, node.RxnMZ):
59	            if "Combo 1" in field:
60	                reactions.append(_scalar(field["Combo 1"]))
61	    disp = np.asarray(displacements, dtype=float)
62	    rxn = np.asarray(reactions, dtype=float)
63	    max_disp = float(np.max(np.abs(disp))) if disp.size and np.isfinite(disp).all() else None
64	    reaction_l1 = float(np.sum(np.abs(rxn))) if rxn.size and np.isfinite(rxn).all() else None
65	    return {
66	        "finite_values": bool(np.isfinite(disp).all() and np.isfinite(rxn).all()),
67	        "max_abs_displacement": max_disp,
68	        "reaction_l1": reaction_l1,
69	        "displacement_count": int(disp.size),
70	    }
71

74	    reports = []

82	            }
83	            try:
84	                getattr(model, method)(sparse=sparse, check_stability=True, check_statics=False)
85	            except Exception as exc:  # a bounded scientific observation
86	                item["status"] = "analysis_exception"

92	                item["status"] = "completed"

1	=========
2	Stability
3	=========
4	
5	Perhaps the trickiest part of finite element modeling is making sure a model is stable. That may
6	sound trivial, but in finite element analysis it is nuanced. If you are getting "singularity"
7	errors in your model, it may not be as stable as you think it is. Remember that just because a
8	model is static does not mean it is stable.
9	
10	Degrees of Freedom
11	==================
12	In 3 dimensions there are 6 "degrees of freedom" for motion to occur in. An object can translate
13	in either the X, Y or Z direction, and it can rotate about the X, Y or Z axis. These 3 translations
14	and 3 rotations together sum to 6 degrees of freedom. For an object to be stable, all 6 degrees
15	of freedom need to be stabilized
16	
17	Instability Type 1: Rigid Body Motion
18	=====================================
19	Rigid body motion occurs when the entire structure can move as a unit in one of the 6 degrees of
20	freedom. This occurs when there is insufficient support for the structure. When rigid body motion
21	occurs, the stiffness matrix is "singular", and unsolvable. Adding supports can eliminate this type
22	of singularity.
23	
24	Instability Type 2: Nodal Instability
25	=====================================
26	Once the global structure is stabilized, there may still be localized instabilities within it. Just
27	as all 6 degrees of freedom need to be constrained at the global level, so do instabilities at the
28	nodal (local) level need to be constrained. These types of instabilities also show up as
29	"singularities" in the stiffness matrix.
30	
31	Consider a truss with multiple hinged-ended members framing into a node. What's to stop the node
32	from spinning if all the members it's attached to are hinged? The correct way to model this joint
33	would be to leave one of the member ends at the node unhinged. Rotations at the node would be then
34	be restrained by that member. It may be that there are no rotations at the node, but the degree of freedom
35	still needs to be tethered to a member (or a support) to make the node stable.
36	
37	When selecting which member to tether the rotation to, consider what the connection looks like in
38	real life. If you were to apply a moment to the joint, where would it go? Unless you're dealing with
39	true pins, it will go somewhere. Even true pins are not frictionless (I've never seen them
40	perpetually rotating in the real world), and you may as well pick which member you want to assign
41	stray forces at that degree of freedom to.
42	
43	Pynite can help you isolate these types of instabilities by passing ``check_stability=True`` to
44	any of the analysis methods (see below for an example). Note that this does slow down analysis, so
45	you usually only want to do this when you are debugging a model.
46	
47	.. code-block:: python
48	
49	    my_model.analyze(check_stability=True)
50	
51	Instability Type 3: Second Order Effects
52	========================================
53	Once the Type 1 and Type 2 instabilities are rooted out of your model, there may be a third type of instability lurking quietly inside it. These types of instabilities can go unnoticed without careful attention to the analysis procedure.
54	
55	Most material codes recognize that a first-order analysis is often not enough. As a structure deforms under load, the geometry changes, making the analysis results invalid. This requires us to reanalyze the structure under the new deformed geometry.
56	
57	The P-:math:`\Delta` analysis feature is one tool Pynite provides to help check for this type of instability. P-:math:`\Delta` analysis is but one piece of the overall picture, which is usually defined by the material's building code. Additional considerations are usually necessary to capture this behavior, such as P-:math:`\delta` analysis, material stiffness reductions and notional loads. Note also that Pynite only performs P-:math:`\Delta` analysis for members. P-:math:`\Delta` effects are not considered for plates. See :doc:`PDelta` for more information.
58	
59	Second order effects are usually only critical for models with slender members, or members with high axial loads in the presence of bending moments. If you don't have these types of features in your model, second order effects may be negligible. Consult your building code for specific criteria in making this determination. Either way, running a P-Delta analysis can help identify erorrs in the model you may have been unaware of. A model that cannot pass a P-Delta analysis is often something you don't really want to build.
60

1	========
2	Analysis
3	========
4	
5	`Pynite` offers several analysis options you can choose from. This section will help you identify the anlysis options you want to run.
6	
7	Sparse vs. Dense Solvers
8	========================
9	
10	Each of the analysis options in Pynite allows you to use either a sparse or dense matrix solver. The dense matrix solver stores all the values in the stiffness matrix, whereas the sparse solver only stores non-zero values. Both solvers provide correct solutions, but each will perform differently depending on your model.
11	
12	The sparse solver is the default solver used by Pynite. It is well suited to large models. It uses less memory and solves large models faster. It solves small models slower, but usually the difference is not noticed because the models are small anyway. In order to use it you'll need to have ``Scipy`` installed.
13	
14	You can switch to the dense solver by passing ``sparse=False`` to the analysis method you are using. ``Scipy`` does not need to be installed to use the dense solver. The dense solver is well suited to small models. If you need to repeatedly solve a small model, the dense solver can offer some performance advantages over the sparse solver.
15	
16	General Analysis
17	================
18	
19	Use the ``FEModel3D.analyze()`` method to run a general analysis. This analysis is iterative if there are tension-only or compression-only elements or supports in the model.
20	
21	Linear Analysis
22	===============
23	
24	Linear analysis can be performed by using the ``FEModel3D.analyze_linear()`` method. This method of analysis is very fast, but is limited to models without nonlinear features such as tension-only or compression-only elements and supports, or P-:math:`\Delta` effects. This method only needs to assemble the stiffness matrix once because it uses analytical superposition of forces to generate load combinations. Superposition requires a linear model.
25	
26	P-:math:`\Delta` Analysis
27	=========================
28	
29	P-:math:`\Delta` analysis is required by many building codes for frame structures. It covered in great detail here: :doc:`PDelta`
30	
31	Other Useful Options
32	====================
33	
34	You can pass a few other parameters to each analysis. To check statics use `check_statics=True` in the analysis command. To check stability use the `check_stability=True` option. Note that this option does slow down solution speed.
35

63	    # Decorator marks this helper as not needing class/instance state.
64	    @staticmethod
65	    # Define helper that flattens node DOFs into a single index vector.
66	    def _build_dof_vector(*nodes: Node3D) -> NDArray[np.int64]:
67	        """Returns the flattened list of global DOF indices for the supplied nodes.
68	
69	        Example for a 2-node member:
70	
71	            [i_node*6 + (0..5), j_node*6 + (0..5)] -> 12 indices total.
72	
73	        Once this vector is created we can operate on entire element sub-matrices via
74	        numpy broadcasting, instead of repeating the ``node.ID*6 + local_dof`` math in
75	        Python loops.
76	        """
77	
78	        # Preallocate the DOF array (nodes * 6 DOFs each) as 64-bit ints.
79	        dofs = np.empty(len(nodes)*6, dtype=np.int64)
80	
81	        # Build a template 0..5 array to shift per node.
82	        local = np.arange(6, dtype=np.int64)
83	
84	        # Iterate through each supplied node with its ordinal index.
85	        for i, node in enumerate(nodes):
86	
87	            # Compute the slice start for this node's 6 DOFs.
88	            start = i*6
89	
90	            # Fill the slice with the node's base DOF plus the 0..5 offsets.
91	            dofs[start:start+6] = node.ID*6 + local
92	            
93	        # Hand back the populated DOF vector for downstream use.
94	        return dofs

96	    # Decorator again indicates no self access is needed for sparse conversion helper.
97	    @staticmethod
98	    # Define helper that converts a dense element block into coo-format row/col/data arrays.
99	    def _append_sparse_block(dofs: NDArray[np.int64], block: np.ndarray,
100	                              row_parts: list[np.ndarray], col_parts: list[np.ndarray],
101	                              data_parts: list[np.ndarray]) -> None:
102	        """Converts an element sub-matrix into row/col/data arrays for COO assembly.
103	
104	        Compared to the former nested loops, this function handles the conversion in
105	        three numpy statements:
106	        1. ``rows = repeat(dofs, size)``
107	        2. ``cols = tile(dofs, size)``
108	        3. ``data = block.reshape(-1)``
109	
110	        Optional zero filtering keeps the sparse storage compact.
111	        """
112	
113	        # Ensure we are working with a float ndarray copy of the element block.
114	        block = np.asarray(block, dtype=float)
115	
116	        # Cache the number of DOFs so we know how many row/column pairs we need; the sparse
117	        # COO builder needs every (row, col) pair formed by combining each DOF with
118	        # every other DOF because each element term contributes to one of those pairs.
119	        size = dofs.size
120	
121	        # Flatten the element block into a 1-D vector matching the row/column pairing order so
122	        # ``flat[k]`` lines up with the kth (row, col) pair produced by the repeat/tile step;
123	        # this guarantees each coefficient from the local matrix lands on the
124	        # matching global DOF pair when we append into COO format.
125	        flat = block.reshape(-1)
126	
127	        # Skip work entirely if this block contains only zeros; many elements (like nodal mass
128	        # shells) hand back zero-filled matrices, and filtering them here avoids appending
129	        # useless entries into the sparse accumulator.
130	        nonzero_mask = flat != 0.0
131	
132	        # Return immediately when there is nothing to contribute to the sparse matrix.
133	        if not np.any(nonzero_mask):
134	            return
135	
136	        # Build the repeated row indices for the full set of row/column combinations; repeating
137	        # each DOF ``size`` times yields the row portion of every (row, col) pair needed for COO insertion.
138	        rows = np.repeat(dofs, size)
139	        
140	        # Build the tiled column indices for that same set of combinations; tiling the DOF vector
141	        # produces the matching column portion for those same (row, col) pairs.
142	        cols = np.tile(dofs, size)
143	
144	        # Append the nonzero row vector to the running parts list.
145	        row_parts.append(rows[nonzero_mask])
146	
147	        # Append the nonzero column vector to the running parts list.
148	        col_parts.append(cols[nonzero_mask])
149	        
150	        # Append the nonzero data values to the running parts list.
151	        data_parts.append(flat[nonzero_mask])

153	    # Decorator marks this helper as purely functional for dense updates.
154	    @staticmethod
155	    # Define helper that adds an element block to the dense global matrix via vectorized indices.
156	    def _add_dense_block(global_matrix: np.ndarray, dofs: NDArray[np.int64], block: np.ndarray) -> None:
157	        """Adds an element block to the dense global matrix using vectorized indexing.
158	
159	        ``np.ix_(dofs, dofs)`` builds every row/column combination of those DOFs, letting the
160	        12x12 or 24x24 block be summed in a single vectorized add.
161	        """
162	
163	        # Convert the block to a float ndarray so dtype math aligns with the global matrix.
164	        block = np.asarray(block, dtype=float)
165	
166	        # Use numpy advanced indexing to add the entire block in one statement.
167	        global_matrix[np.ix_(dofs, dofs)] += block

169	    @property
170	    def load_cases(self) -> List[str]:
171	        """Returns a list of all the load cases in the model (in alphabetical order).
172	        """
173	
174	        # Create an empty list of load cases
175	        cases: List[str] = []
176	
177	        # Step through each node
178	        for node in self.nodes.values():
179	            # Step through each nodal load
180	            for load in node.NodeLoads:
181	                # Get the load case for each nodal laod
182	                cases.append(load[2])
183	
184	        # Step through each member
185	        for member in self.members.values():
186	            # Step through each member point load
187	            for load in member.PtLoads:
188	                # Get the load case for each member point load
189	                cases.append(load[3])
190	            # Step through each member distributed load
191	            for load in member.DistLoads:
192	                # Get the load case for each member distributed load
193	                cases.append(load[5])
194	
195	        # Step through each plate/quad
196	        for plate in list(self.plates.values()) + list(self.quads.values()):
197	            # Step through each surface load
198	            for load in plate.pressures:
199	                # Get the load case for each plate/quad pressure
200	                cases.append(load[1])
201	
202	        # Step through each shear wall helper
203	        for shear_wall in self.shear_walls.values():
204	            # Step through each shear wall shear load
205	            for load in shear_wall._shears:
206	                # Get the load case for each shear wall shear
207	                cases.append(load[2])
208	
209	            # Step through each shear wall axial load
210	            for load in shear_wall._axials:
211	                # Get the load case for each shear wall axial
212	                cases.append(load[2])
213	
214	        # Step through each mat foundation helper
215	        for mat in self.mats.values():
216	            # Step through each mat point load
217	            for load in mat.pt_loads:
218	                # Get the load case for each mat point load
219	                cases.append(load[3])
220	
221	        # Remove duplicates and return the list (sorted ascending)
222	        return sorted(list(dict.fromkeys(cases)))

953	    def merge_duplicate_nodes(self, tolerance: float = 0.001) -> list:
954	        """Removes duplicate nodes from the model and returns a list of the removed node names.
955	
956	        :param tolerance: The maximum distance between two nodes in order to consider them duplicates. Defaults to 0.001.
957	        :type tolerance: float, optional
958	        :return: A list of the names of the nodes that were removed from the model.
959	        """
960	
961	        # Initialize a dictionary marking where each node is used
962	        node_lookup = {node_name: [] for node_name in self.nodes.keys()}
963	        element_dicts = ('springs', 'members', 'plates', 'quads')
964	        node_types = ('i_node', 'j_node', 'm_node', 'n_node')
965	
966	        # Step through each dictionary of elements in the model (springs, members, plates, quads)
967	        for element_dict in element_dicts:
968	
969	            # Step through each element in the dictionary
970	            for element in getattr(self, element_dict).values():
971	
972	                # Step through each possible node type in the element (i-node, j-node, m-node, n-node)
973	                for node_type in node_types:
974	
975	                    # Get the current element's node having the current type
976	                    # Return `None` if the element doesn't have this node type
977	                    node = getattr(element, node_type, None)
978	
979	                    # Determine if the node exists on the element
980	                    if node is not None:
981	                        # Add the element to the list of elements attached to the node
982	                        node_lookup[node.name].append((element, node_type))
983	
984	        # Make a list of the names of each node in the model
985	        node_names = list(self.nodes.keys())
986	
987	        # Make a list of nodes to be removed from the model
988	        remove_list = []
989	
990	        # Step through each node in the copy of the `Nodes` dictionary
991	        for i, node_1_name in enumerate(node_names):
992	
993	            # Skip iteration if `node_1` has already been removed
994	            if node_lookup[node_1_name] is None:
995	                continue
996	
997	            # There is no need to check `node_1` against itself
998	            for node_2_name in node_names[i + 1:]:
999	
1000	                # Skip iteration if node_2 has already been removed
1001	                if node_lookup[node_2_name] is None:
1002	                    continue
1003	
1004	                # Calculate the distance between nodes
1005	                if self.nodes[node_1_name].distance(self.nodes[node_2_name]) > tolerance:
1006	                    continue
1007	
1008	                # Replace references to `node_2` in each element with references to `node_1`
1009	                for element, node_type in node_lookup[node_2_name]:
1010	                    setattr(element, node_type, self.nodes[node_1_name])
1011	
1012	                # Flag `node_2` as no longer used
1013	                node_lookup[node_2_name] = None
1014	
1015	                # Merge any boundary conditions
1016	                support_cond = ('support_DX', 'support_DY', 'support_DZ', 'support_RX', 'support_RY', 'support_RZ')
1017	                for dof in support_cond:
1018	                    if getattr(self.nodes[node_2_name], dof) == True:
1019	                        setattr(self.nodes[node_1_name], dof, True)

Scipy's documentation states that this type of matrix is ideal for efficient construction of finite element matrices. 2137	        """Assembles and returns the global fixed end reaction vector for any given load combo.

2147	        FER = np.zeros((len(self.nodes) * 6, 1))
2148

2151	        # DOFs without touching individual entries.

2154	            # Step through each sub-member and add terms

2170	            dofs = self._build_dof_vector(plate.i_node, plate.j_node, plate.m_node, plate.n_node)
2171	            FER[dofs, 0] += plate_FER

2173	        # Quadrilaterals follow the same pattern: 24x1 block dropped in via the DOF helper.
2174	        for quad in self.quads.values():

2184	    def P(self, combo_name='Combo 1') -> NDArray[float64]:
2185	        """Assembles and returns the global nodal force vector.
2186	
2187	        :param combo_name: The name of the load combination to get the force vector for. Defaults
2188	                           to 'Combo 1'.
2189	        :type combo_name: str, optional
2190	        :return: The global nodal force vector.
2191	        :rtype: NDArray[float64]
2192	        """
2193	
2194	        # Initialize a zero vector to hold all the terms
2195	        P = np.zeros((len(self.nodes)*6, 1))
2196	
2197	        # Get the load combination for the given 'combo_name'
2198	        combo = self.load_combos[combo_name]
2199	
2200	        # Map load direction strings to their DOF offsets once so we do not re-run the
2201	        # if/elif ladder for every single nodal load.
2202	        dof_lookup = {'FX': 0, 'FY': 1, 'FZ': 2, 'MX': 3, 'MY': 4, 'MZ': 5}

2204	        # Add terms for each node in the model

2207	            # Accumulate this node's six DOF loads locally before writing to the global vector.
2208	            # This keeps the code vectorized and avoids hammering the global array for every
2209	            # individual load tuple.
2210	            local = np.zeros(6, dtype=float)
2211	
2212	            for direction, magnitude, case in node.NodeLoads:
2213	                # Look up the combo factor once per load; loads from unrelated cases are skipped
2214	                # immediately instead of falling through nested conditionals.
2215	                factor = combo.factors.get(case)
2216	                if factor is None:

2218	
2219	                # Normalize the direction string and map it to the correct DOF slot. Unknown
2220	                # direction labels are ignored to match the previous behavior.
2221	                idx = dof_lookup.get(direction.upper())
2222	                if idx is None:

2225	                # Add the scaled load into the local 6-entry accumulator.
2226	                local[idx] += factor * magnitude

2228	            # Once all loads for this node are tallied, drop the 6x1 block into the global

2230	            if np.any(local):

2232	                P[dofs, 0] += local
2233

2235	        return P

2477	    def analyze_modal(self, num_modes: int = 12, mass_combo_name: str = 'Combo 1', mass_direction: str = 'Y', gravity: float = 1.0, log=False, check_stability=True):
2478	        """
2479	        Performs modal analysis to determine natural frequencies and mode shapes.
2480	
2481	        A sparse solution based on `num_modes` is always used to help filter out irrelevant frequencies from unimportant modes.
2482	
2483	        :param num_modes: Number of modes to calculate. Defaults to 12.
2484	        :type num_modes: int, optional
2485	        :param mass_combo_name: Load combination name to use to convert loads to masses. Defaults to `Combo 1`.
2486	        :type mass_combo_name: str, optional
2487	        :param mass_direction: Direction for load-to-mass conversion ('X', 'Y', or 'Z'). Any loads applied in this direction (postive or negative) will be converted to mass. Defaults to 'Y'.
2488	        :type mass_direction: str, optional
2489	        :param gravity: The acceleration due to gravity. Defaults to 1.0. In most cases you'll want to change this to be in units consistent with your model.
2490	        :type gravity: float
2491	        :param log: Prints the analysis log to the console if set to True. Default is False.
2492	        :type log: bool, optional
2493	        :param check_stability: When set to True, checks the stiffness matrix for unstable DOFs. Defaults to True.
2494	        :type check_stability: bool, optional
2495	        :return: A list containing frequencies (Hz)
2496	        :rtype: List
2497	        :raises Exception: Occurs when a singular stiffness matrix is found.
2498	        """
2499	
2500	        if log:
2501	            print('+------------------+')
2502	            print('| Analyzing: Modal |')
2503	            print('+------------------+')
2504	
2505	        # Prepare the model for analysis (same as other analysis methods)
2506	        # This will generate the default load case ('Case 1') and load combo ('Combo 1') if none are present.
2507	        Analysis._prepare_model(self, num_modes)
2508	
2509	        # Get the auxiliary list used for matrix partitioning
2510	        D1_indices, D2_indices, D2 = Analysis._partition_D(self)
2511	
2512	        if log:
2513	            print('- Assembling global stiffness matrix')
2514	
2515	        # Assemble and partition the global stiffness matrix
2516	        Ke_global = self.Ke(mass_combo_name, log, check_stability, sparse=True).tocsr()
2517	
2518	        # Partition to remove supported DOFs
2519	        K11, K12, K21, K22 = Analysis._partition(self, Ke_global, D1_indices, D2_indices)
2520	
2521	        if log:
2522	            print('- Assembling global mass matrix')
2523	
2524	        # Assemble and partition the global mass matrix
2525	        M_global = self.M(mass_combo_name, mass_direction, gravity, log, sparse=True).tocsr()
2526	
2527	        # Partition to remove supported DOFs
2528	        M11, M12, M21, M22 = Analysis._partition(self, M_global, D1_indices, D2_indices)
2529	
2530	        # Check that we have mass terms
2531	        if M11.nnz == 0:
2532	            raise Exception('No mass terms found. Ensure materials have density or provide mass_combo_name.')
2533	
2534	        if log:
2535	            print('- Solving eigenvalue problem')
2536	
2537	        try:
2538	            # Solve the generalized eigenvalue problem: [K11]{φ} = λ[M11]{φ}, where λ = ω²
2539	            # Or rewritten: (-[M11]ω² + [K11]){φ} = 0
2540	            # (See "Structural Dynamics for Structural Engineers" by Hart & Wong Equation 4.96)
2541	            eigenvalues, eigenvectors = sp.sparse.linalg.eigsh(A=K11, k=num_modes, M=M11, sigma=0.0, which='LM')
2542	
2543	        except sp.linalg.LinAlgError as e:
2544	            raise Exception(f'Eigenvalue solution failed: {str(e)}. Check matrix conditioning.')
2545	
2546	        # Calculate frequencies in Hz from eigenvalues (λ = ω²)
2547	        frequencies = np.sqrt(eigenvalues) / (2 * np.pi)
2548	
2549	        if log:
2550	            print('- Processing mode shapes')
2551	
2552	        # Process eigenvectors (mode shapes) to expand back to full DOF set
2553	        for i in range(len(frequencies)):
2554	
2555	            # Get the load combo for this mode
2556	            mode_combo = self.load_combos[f'Mode {i + 1}']
2557	
2558	            # Reshape the SciPy eigenvector (mode shape) into a column array that is compatible with Pynite
2559	            D1_mode = eigenvectors[:, i].reshape(-1, 1)
2560	
2561	            Analysis._store_displacements(self, D1_mode, D2, D1_indices, D2_indices, mode_combo)
2562	
2563	        # Store results in the model
2564	        self.frequencies = frequencies
2565	
2566	        if log:
2567	            print('- Modal analysis complete')
2568	
2569	        # Flag the model as having modal results
2570	        self.solution = 'Modal'
2571	
2572	        if log:
2573	            print(f'- Found {len(frequencies)} modes')
2574	            for i, freq in enumerate(frequencies):
2575	                print(f'  Mode {i + 1}: {freq:.3f} Hz')
2576	            print('- Modal analysis complete')

2660	    def analyze_pushover(self, log=False, check_stability=True, push_combo='Push', max_iter=30, tol=0.01, sparse=True, combo_tags=None, control_node=None, control_direction='DX', control_limit=None, traces=None):

2665	        pushover API currently does not expose a P-Delta option until the implementation is
2666	        production-ready.

2686	        :type control_node: str | None, optional

2688	        :type control_direction: str, optional

2690	        :type control_limit: float | None, optional

2715	                    )

2720	            print('+---------------------+')

2723	        Analysis._prepare_model(self)

2789	                    sub_member._myi[combo.name] = f[4, 0]
2790	                    sub_member._mzi[combo.name] = f[5, 0]
2791	                    sub_member._fxj[combo.name] = f[6, 0]
2792	                    sub_member._fyj[combo.name] = f[7, 0]
2793	                    sub_member._fzj[combo.name] = f[8, 0]

2802

2901	    def unique_name(self, dictionary, prefix):
2902	        """Returns the next available unique name for a dictionary of objects.
2903	
2904	        :param dictionary: The dictionary to get a unique name for.
2905	        :type dictionary: dict
2906	        :param prefix: The prefix to use for the unique name.
2907	        :type prefix: str
2908	        :return: A unique name for the dictionary.
2909	        :rtype: str
2910	        """
2911	
2912	        # Select a trial value for the next available name
2913	        name = prefix + str(len(dictionary) + 1)
2914	        i = 2
2915	        while name in dictionary.keys():
2916	            name = prefix + str(len(dictionary) + i)
2917	            i += 1
2918	
2919	        # Return the next available name
2920	        return name

472	            if log: print('Calculating plastic reduction matrix [Km]')
473	            Km11, Km12, Km21, Km22 = _partition(model, model.Km(combo_name, push_combo, step_num, log, sparse), D1_indices, D2_indices)
474	
475	            K11 = Ke11 + Km11
476	            K12 = Ke12 + Km12
477	            # K21 = Ke21 + Km21  # This matrix is not used
478	            # K22 = Ke22 + Km22  # This matrix is not used
479	
480	            if P_Delta:
481	                # The `combo_name` variable in the code below is not the name of the pushover load combination. Rather it is the name of the primary combination that the pushover load will be added to. Axial loads used to develop Kg are calculated from the displacements stored in `combo_name`.
482	                if log: print('Calculating geometric stiffness matrix [Kg]')
483	                Kg11, Kg12, Kg21, Kg22 = _partition(model, model.Kg(combo_name, log, sparse, False), D1_indices, D2_indices)
484	                K11 = K11 + Kg11
485	                K12 = K12 + Kg12
486	                # K21 = K21 + Kg21  # This matrix is not used
487	                # K22 = K22 + Kg22  # This matrix is not used
488	
489	        # Calculate the changes to the global displacement vector
490	        if log: print('- Calculating changes to the global displacement vector')
491	        if K11.shape == (0, 0):
492	            # All displacements are known, so D1 is an empty vector
493	            Delta_D1 = []
494	        else:
495	            try:
496	                # Calculate the change in the displacements Delta_D1
497	                if sparse == True:
498	                    # The partitioned stiffness matrix is already in `csr` format. The `@`
499	                    # operator performs matrix multiplication on sparse matrices.
500	                    Delta_D1 = spsolve(K11.tocsr(), subtract(subtract(Delta_P1, Delta_FER1), K12.tocsr() @ D2))
501	                    Delta_D1 = Delta_D1.reshape(len(Delta_D1), 1)
502	                else:
503	                    # The partitioned stiffness matrix is in `csr` format. It will be
504	                    # converted to a 2D dense array for mathematical operations.
505	                    Delta_D1 = solve(K11, subtract(subtract(Delta_P1, Delta_FER1), K12 @ D2))
506	
507	            except:
508	                # Return out of the method if 'K' is singular and provide an error message
509	                raise ValueError('The structure is unstable. Unable to proceed any further with analysis.')
510	
511	        # Tentatively apply the load step so step-validation checks see the current state.
512	        _sum_displacements(model, Delta_D1, D2, D1_indices, D2_indices, model.load_combos[combo_name])
513	
514	        # Assume no need to rerun this load step until one of the validation checks says otherwise.
515	        run_step = False
516	        tc_changed = False
517	        reversal = False
518	        reversal_locations = []
519	
520	        # Check for tension/compression-only status changes caused by this tentative load step.
521	        if _check_TC_convergence(model, combo_name, log, spring_tolerance=tol, member_tolerance=tol) == False:
522	            tc_changed = True
523	            run_step = True
524	
525	        # Unpartition the displacement results from the analysis step for the `lamb` calculations below
526	        Delta_D = _unpartition(model, Delta_D1, D2, D1_indices, D2_indices)
527	        Delta_FER = _unpartition(model, Delta_FER1, Delta_FER2, D1_indices, D2_indices)
528	
529	        # Step through each member in the model and check for plastic load reversal.
530	        for phys_member in model.members.values():
531	
532	            for sub_member in phys_member.sub_members.values():
533	
534	                lamb = sub_member.lamb(Delta_D, combo_name, push_combo, step_num)
535	
536	                # Check for plastic load reversal at the i-node in this load step
537	                if lamb[0, 0] < 0:
538	
539	                    # Flag the load step for reanalysis
540	                    sub_member.i_reversal = True
541	                    reversal = True
542	                    run_step = True
543	                    reversal_locations.append(f'{sub_member.name} i-node')
544	                    if log: print(f'- Plastic load reversal encountered at member {sub_member.name} i-node')
545	
546	                else:
547	
548	                    sub_member.i_reversal = False
549	
550	                # Check for plastic load reversal at the j-node in this load step
551	                if lamb[1, 0] < 0:
552	
553	                    # Flag the load step for reanalysis
554	                    sub_member.j_reversal = True
555	                    reversal = True
556	                    run_step = True
557	                    reversal_locations.append(f'{sub_member.name} j-node')
558	                    if log: print(f'- Plastic load reversal encountered at member {sub_member.name} j-node')
559	
560	                else:
561	
562	                    sub_member.j_reversal = False
563	
564	        # Check if this iteration was valid
565	        if run_step == False:
566	
567	            # Step through each physical member in the model
568	            for phys_member in model.members.values():
569	
570	                # Step through each sub-member of the physical member
571	                for sub_member in phys_member.sub_members.values():
572	
573	                    # Extract the change in the global displacement and fixed end reaction vectors for this member from the full global vectors. The `reshape` method is used to ensure these are column vectors for the matrix operations below.
574	                    Delta_D_member = array([Delta_D[sub_member.i_node.ID*6 + 0, 0],
575	                                            Delta_D[sub_member.i_node.ID*6 + 1, 0],
576	                                            Delta_D[sub_member.i_node.ID*6 + 2, 0],
577	                                            Delta_D[sub_member.i_node.ID*6 + 3, 0],
578	                                            Delta_D[sub_member.i_node.ID*6 + 4, 0],
579	                                            Delta_D[sub_member.i_node.ID*6 + 5, 0],
580	                                            Delta_D[sub_member.j_node.ID*6 + 0, 0],
581	                                            Delta_D[sub_member.j_node.ID*6 + 1, 0],
582	                                            Delta_D[sub_member.j_node.ID*6 + 2, 0],
583	                                            Delta_D[sub_member.j_node.ID*6 + 3, 0],
584	                                            Delta_D[sub_member.j_node.ID*6 + 4, 0],
585	                                            Delta_D[sub_member.j_node.ID*6 + 5, 0]]).reshape(12, 1)
586	                    
587	                    Delta_FER_member = array([Delta_FER[sub_member.i_node.ID*6 + 0, 0],
588	                                              Delta_FER[sub_member.i_node.ID*6 + 1, 0],
589	                                              Delta_FER[sub_member.i_node.ID*6 + 2, 0],
590	                                              Delta_FER[sub_member.i_node.ID*6 + 3, 0],
591	                                              Delta_FER[sub_member.i_node.ID*6 + 4, 0],
592	                                              Delta_FER[sub_member.i_node.ID*6 + 5, 0],
593	                                              Delta_FER[sub_member.j_node.ID*6 + 0, 0],
594	                                              Delta_FER[sub_member.j_node.ID*6 + 1, 0],
595	                                              Delta_FER[sub_member.j_node.ID*6 + 2, 0],
596	                                              Delta_FER[sub_member.j_node.ID*6 + 3, 0],
597	                                              Delta_FER[sub_member.j_node.ID*6 + 4, 0],
598	                                              Delta_FER[sub_member.j_node.ID*6 + 5, 0]]).reshape(12, 1)
599	                    
600	                    # Convert the global displacement and fixed end reaction vectors to local member vectors
601	                    Delta_d = sub_member.T() @ Delta_D_member
602	                    Delta_fer = sub_member.T() @ Delta_FER_member
603	
604	                    # Calculate change in the local end force vector for this load step
605	                    Delta_f = sub_member.f(combo_name, Delta_d, Delta_fer)
606	                    
607	                    sub_member._fxi[combo_name] += Delta_f[0, 0]
608	                    sub_member._fyi[combo_name] += Delta_f[1, 0]
609	                    sub_member._fzi[combo_name] += Delta_f[2, 0]
610	                    sub_member._mxi[combo_name] += Delta_f[3, 0]
611	                    sub_member._myi[combo_name] += Delta_f[4, 0]
612	                    sub_member._mzi[combo_name] += Delta_f[5, 0]
613	                    sub_member._fxj[combo_name] += Delta_f[6, 0]
614	                    sub_member._fyj[combo_name] += Delta_f[7, 0]
615	                    sub_member._fzj[combo_name] += Delta_f[8, 0]
616	                    sub_member._mxj[combo_name] += Delta_f[9, 0]
617	                    sub_member._myj[combo_name] += Delta_f[10, 0]
618	                    sub_member._mzj[combo_name] += Delta_f[11, 0]
619	
620	        else:
621	
622	            tc_changed_last = tc_changed
623	            reversal_locations_last = list(dict.fromkeys(reversal_locations))
624	
625	            # Undo the tentative load step
626	            _sum_displacements(model, -Delta_D1, D2, D1_indices, D2_indices, model.load_combos[combo_name])
627	            if log:
628	                if tc_changed and reversal:
629	                    print('- Restarting load step due to tension/compression-only status change and plastic load reversal')
630	                elif tc_changed:
631	                    print('- Restarting load step due to tension/compression-only status change')
632	                else:
633	                    print('- Restarting load step due to plastic load reversal')

636	def _unpartition(model: FEModel3D, V1: NDArray[float64], V2: NDArray[float64], V1_indices: List[int], V2_indices: List[int]) -> NDArray[float64]:
637	    """Unpartitions a vector and returns it as a global vector including all dofs.
638	
639	    :param model: The finite element model being evaluated
640	    :type model: FEModel3D
641	    :param V1: An array of vector terms corresponding to the unrestrained degrees of freedom.
642	    :type V1: array
643	    :param V2: An array of vector terms corresponding to the degrees of freedom with boundary conditions.
644	    :type V2: array
645	    :param V1_indices: A list of the degree of freedom indices for each term in V1
646	    :type V1_indices: list
647	    :param V2_indices: A list of the degree of freedom indices for each term in V2
648	    :type V2_indices: list
649	    :return: Expanded vector
650	    :rtype: array
651	    """
652	
653	    V = zeros((len(model.nodes)*6, 1))
654	
655	    # Step through each node in the model
656	    for node in model.nodes.values():
657	
658	        # Step through each degree of freedom at the node
659	        for i in range(6):
660	
661	            # Check if the dof is in the list of known vector terms
662	            if node.ID*6 + i in V2_indices:
663	                # Get the vector term for the bounded dof
664	                V[(node.ID*6 + i, 0)] = V2[V2_indices.index(node.ID*6 + i), 0]
665	            else:
666	                # Get the vector term for the unbounded dof
667	                V[(node.ID*6 + i, 0)] = V1[V1_indices.index(node.ID*6 + i), 0]
668	
669	    # Return the vector
670	    return V

673	def _store_displacements(model: FEModel3D, D1: NDArray[float64], D2: NDArray[float64], D1_indices: List[int], D2_indices: List[int], combo: LoadCombo) -> None:
674	    """Stores calculated displacements from the solver into the model's displacement vector `_D` and into each node object in the model
675	
676	    :param model: The finite element model being evaluated.
677	    :type model: FEModel3D
678	    :param D1: An array of calculated displacements
679	    :type D1: array
680	    :param D2: An array of enforced displacements
681	    :type D2: array
682	    :param D1_indices: A list of the degree of freedom indices for each displacement in D1
683	    :type D1_indices: list
684	    :param D2_indices: A list of the degree of freedom indices for each displacement in D2
685	    :type D2_indices: list
686	    :param combo: The load combination to store the displacements for.
687	    :type combo: LoadCombo
688	    """
689	
690	    # The raw results from the solver are partitioned. Unpartition them.
691	    D = _unpartition(model, D1, D2, D1_indices, D2_indices)
692	
693	    if combo != None:
694	
695	        # Store the displacements in the model's global displacement vector
696	        model._D[combo.name] = D
697	
698	        # Store the calculated global nodal displacements into each node object
699	        for node in model.nodes.values():
700	
701	            node.DX[combo.name] = D[node.ID*6 + 0, 0]
702	            node.DY[combo.name] = D[node.ID*6 + 1, 0]
703	            node.DZ[combo.name] = D[node.ID*6 + 2, 0]
704	            node.RX[combo.name] = D[node.ID*6 + 3, 0]
705	            node.RY[combo.name] = D[node.ID*6 + 4, 0]
706	            node.RZ[combo.name] = D[node.ID*6 + 5, 0]

709	def _sum_displacements(model: FEModel3D, Delta_D1: NDArray[float64], Delta_D2: NDArray[float64], D1_indices: List[int], D2_indices: List[int], combo: LoadCombo) -> None:
710	    """Sums calculated displacements for a load step from the solver into the model's displacement vector `_D` and into each node object in the model.
711	
712	    :param model: The finite element model being evaluated.
713	    :type model: FEModel3D
714	    :param Delta_D1: An array of calculated displacements for a load step
715	    :type Delta_D1: array
716	    :param Delta_D2: An array of enforced displacements for a load step
717	    :type Delta_D2: array
718	    :param D1_indices: A list of the degree of freedom indices for each displacement in D1
719	    :type D1_indices: list
720	    :param D2_indices: A list of the degree of freedom indices for each displacement in D2
721	    :type D2_indices: list
722	    :param combo: The load combination to store the displacements for
723	    :type combo: LoadCombo
724	    """
725	
726	    # The raw results from the solver are partitioned. Unpartition them.
727	    Delta_D = _unpartition(model, Delta_D1, Delta_D2, D1_indices, D2_indices)
728	
729	    # Sum the load step's global displacement vector with the model's global displacement vector
730	    model._D[combo.name] += Delta_D
731	
732	    # Sum the load step's calculated global nodal displacements to each node object's global displacement
733	    for node in model.nodes.values():
734	
735	        node.DX[combo.name] += Delta_D[node.ID*6 + 0, 0]
736	        node.DY[combo.name] += Delta_D[node.ID*6 + 1, 0]
737	        node.DZ[combo.name] += Delta_D[node.ID*6 + 2, 0]
738	        node.RX[combo.name] += Delta_D[node.ID*6 + 3, 0]
739	        node.RY[combo.name] += Delta_D[node.ID*6 + 4, 0]
740	        node.RZ[combo.name] += Delta_D[node.ID*6 + 5, 0]

743	def _check_TC_convergence(model: FEModel3D, combo_name: str = "Combo 1", log: bool = True, spring_tolerance: float = 0, member_tolerance: float = 0) -> bool:
744	    """Checks for convergence in tension-only and compression-only analysis.
745	
746	    This function evaluates the status of tension-only and compression-only springs and members
747	    within the finite element model for a given load combination. Its primary purpose is to
748	    determine if the non-linear analysis has converged by checking if any adjustments to the
749	    active status of these elements are required.
750	
751	    The function performs the following checks:
752	    *   **Nodal Spring Convergence**: It iterates through each nodal spring and assesses whether
753	        its active state (whether it is resisting force) aligns with the current displacement
754	        and its tension-only or compression-only designation. If a spring's active
755	        status needs to change based on the displacement and a specified tolerance, the analysis
756	        is flagged as not converged, and the spring's `active` status is updated.
757	    *   **Member Convergence**: It checks each physical member in the model. If a
758	        tension-only member is active but has a maximum axial force greater than the
759	        `member_tolerance` (indicating compression), or if a compression-only member is active
760	        but has a minimum axial force less than `-member_tolerance` (indicating tension),
761	        that physical member and all its sub-members are deactivated. This action
762	        flags the analysis as not converged. A future enhancement is noted to allow elements to
763	        reactivate if deformations indicate they should return to an active state.
764	    *   **Sub-member Reset**: After checking, the `_solved_combo` flag for all sub-members is
765	        reset to `None`. This ensures that they will be resegmented and re-evaluated in subsequent
766	        iterations of the analysis, allowing for further changes as needed for convergence.
767	
768	    :param model: The finite element model currently being evaluated.
769	    :type model: FEModel3D
770	    :param combo_name: The name of the load combination for which the convergence check is
771	        being performed. Defaults to "Combo 1".
772	    :type combo_name: str, optional
773	    :param log: A boolean flag. If `True`, the function prints status updates and information
774	        about the convergence check to the console. Defaults to `True`.
775	    :type log: bool, optional
776	    :param spring_tolerance: A float value representing the displacement tolerance for
777	        tension/compression-only support springs. Springs will switch active state if their
778	        displacement is beyond this tolerance in the disallowed direction. Defaults to 0.
779	    :type spring_tolerance: float, optional
780	    :param member_tolerance: A float value representing the axial force tolerance for
781	        tension/compression-only members. Members will be deactivated if their axial force
782	        is beyond this tolerance in the disallowed direction. Defaults to 0.
783	    :type member_tolerance: float, optional
784	    :return: **True** if all tension-only and compression-only elements have converged (no
785	        changes in active status are needed), **False** otherwise (indicating that further
786	        iterations of the analysis are required).
787	    :rtype: bool
788	    """
789	
790	    # Assume the model has converged until we find out otherwise
791	    convergence = True
792	
793	    # Provide an update to the console if requested by the user
794	    if log:
795	        print("- Checking for tension/compression-only support spring convergence")
796	
797	    # Loop through each node and each directional spring to check and update their active status
798	    for node in model.nodes.values():
799	
800	        for direction in ["DX", "DY", "DZ", "RX", "RY", "RZ"]:
801	            spring = getattr(node, f"spring_{direction}")
802	            displacement = getattr(node, direction)[combo_name]
803	
804	            if spring[1] is not None:
805	                # Determine if the spring should be active based on its designation ('+' or '-') and the displacement
806	                should_be_active = (
807	                    spring[1] == "-" and displacement <= -spring_tolerance
808	                ) or (spring[1] == "+" and displacement >= spring_tolerance)
809	
810	                # Check if there's a need to switch the active state of the spring
811	                if spring[2] != should_be_active:
812	                    spring[2] = should_be_active
813	                    convergence = False
814	
815	    # TODO: Adjust the code below to allow elements to reactivate on subsequent iterations if deformations at element nodes indicate the member goes back into an active state. This will lead to a less conservative and more realistic analysis. Nodal springs (above) already do this.
816	
817	    # Check tension/compression-only springs
818	    if log:
819	        print('- Checking for tension/compression-only spring convergence')
820	
821	    for spring in model.springs.values():
822	
823	        if spring.active[combo_name] == True:
824	
825	            # Check if tension-only conditions exist
826	            if (spring.tension_only == True) and (spring.axial(combo_name) > spring_tolerance):
827	                if log:
828	                    print(f'- Deactivating spring {spring.name}')
829	                spring.active[combo_name] = False
830	                convergence = False
831	
832	            # Check if compression-only conditions exist
833	            elif (spring.comp_only == True) and (spring.axial(combo_name) < -spring_tolerance):
834	                if log:
835	                    print(f'- Deactivating spring {spring.name}')
836	                spring.active[combo_name] = False
837	                convergence = False
838	
839	    # Check tension/compression only members
840	    if log:
841	        print('- Checking for tension/compression-only member convergence')
842	    for phys_member in model.members.values():
843	
844	        # Only run the tension/compression only check if the member is still active
845	        if phys_member.active[combo_name] == True:
846	
847	            # Check if a tension-only conditions exist
848	            if phys_member.tension_only == True and phys_member.max_axial(combo_name) > member_tolerance:
849	
850	                # Deactivate the physical member
851	                if log:
852	                    print(f'- Deactivating member {phys_member.name}')
853	                phys_member.active[combo_name] = False
854	
855	                # Deactivate all the sub-members
856	                for sub_member in phys_member.sub_members.values():
857	                    sub_member.active[combo_name] = False
858	
859	                # Flag the analysis as not converged
860	                convergence = False
861	
862	            # Check if a compression-only conditions exist
863	            elif phys_member.comp_only == True and phys_member.min_axial(combo_name) < - member_tolerance:
864	
865	                # Deactivate the physical member
866	                if log:
867	                    print(f'- Deactivating member {phys_member.name}')
868	                phys_member.active[combo_name] = False
869	
870	                # Deactivate all the sub-members
871	                for sub_member in phys_member.sub_members.values():
872	                    sub_member.active[combo_name] = False
873	
874	                # Flag the analysis as not converged
875	                convergence = False
876	
877	        # Reset the sub-member's flag to unsolved. This will allow it to resolve for the same load combination after subsequent iterations have made further changes.
878	        for sub_member in phys_member.sub_members.values():
879	            sub_member._solved_combo = None
880	
881	    # Return whether the TC analysis has converged
882	    return convergence

885	def _calc_reactions(model: FEModel3D, log: bool = False, combo_tags: List[str] | None = None) -> None:
886	    """
887	    Calculates reactions internally once the model is solved.
888	
889	    Parameters
890	    ----------
891	    model : FEModel3D
892	        The finite element model to calculate reactions for.
893	    log : bool, optional
894	        Prints updates to the console if set to True. Default == False.
895	    combo_tags : string, optional
896	        A list of tags that will be used to identify which load combinations need their reactions calculated. If set to `None` then all load combinations will have their reactions calculated. Default is `None`.
897	    """
898	
899	    # Print a status update to the console
900	    if log:
901	        print('- Calculating reactions')
902	
903	    # Identify which load combinations to evaluate
904	    combo_list = _identify_combos(model, combo_tags)
905	
906	    # Calculate the reactions node by node
907	    for node in model.nodes.values():
908	
909	        # Step through each load combination
910	        for combo in combo_list:
911	
912	            # Initialize reactions for this node and load combination
913	            node.RxnFX[combo.name] = 0.0
914	            node.RxnFY[combo.name] = 0.0
915	            node.RxnFZ[combo.name] = 0.0
916	            node.RxnMX[combo.name] = 0.0
917	            node.RxnMY[combo.name] = 0.0
918	            node.RxnMZ[combo.name] = 0.0
919	
920	            # Determine if the node has any supports
921	            if (node.support_DX or node.support_DY or node.support_DZ
922	            or  node.support_RX or node.support_RY or node.support_RZ):
923	
924	                # Sum the spring end forces at the node
925	                for spring in model.springs.values():
926	
927	                    if spring.i_node == node and spring.active[combo.name] == True:
928	
929	                        # Get the spring's global force matrix
930	                        # Storing it as a local variable eliminates the need to rebuild it every time a term is needed
931	                        spring_F = spring.F(combo.name)
932	
933	                        if node.support_DX: node.RxnFX[combo.name] += spring_F[0, 0]
934	                        if node.support_DY: node.RxnFY[combo.name] += spring_F[1, 0]
935	                        if node.support_DZ: node.RxnFZ[combo.name] += spring_F[2, 0]
936	                        if node.support_RX: node.RxnMX[combo.name] += spring_F[3, 0]
937	                        if node.support_RY: node.RxnMY[combo.name] += spring_F[4, 0]
938	                        if node.support_RZ: node.RxnMZ[combo.name] += spring_F[5, 0]
939	
940	                    elif spring.j_node == node and spring.active[combo.name] == True:
941	
942	                        # Get the spring's global force matrix
943	                        # Storing it as a local variable eliminates the need to rebuild it every time a term is needed
944	                        spring_F = spring.F(combo.name)
945

1142	def _check_statics(model: FEModel3D, combo_tags: List[str] | None = None) -> None:
1143	    '''
1144	    Checks static equilibrium and prints results to the console.
1145	
1146	    Parameters
1147	    ----------
1148	    precision : number
1149	        The number of decimal places to carry the results to.
1150	    '''
1151	
1152	    print('+----------------+')
1153	    print('| Statics Check: |')
1154	    print('+----------------+')
1155	    print('')
1156	
1157	    from prettytable import PrettyTable
1158	
1159	    # Start a blank table and create a header row
1160	    statics_table = PrettyTable()
1161	    statics_table.field_names = ['Load Combination', 'Sum FX', 'Sum RX', 'Sum FY', 'Sum RY', 'Sum FZ', 'Sum RZ', 'Sum MX', 'Sum RMX', 'Sum MY', 'Sum RMY', 'Sum MZ', 'Sum RMZ']
1162	
1163	    # Identify which load combinations to evaluate
1164	    if combo_tags is None:
1165	        combo_list = model.load_combos.values()
1166	    else:
1167	        combo_list = []
1168	        for combo in model.load_combos.values():
1169	            if any(tag in combo.combo_tags for tag in combo_tags):
1170	                combo_list.append(combo)
1171	
1172	    # Step through each load combination
1173	    for combo in combo_list:
1174	
1175	        # Initialize force and moment summations to zero
1176	        SumFX, SumFY, SumFZ = 0.0, 0.0, 0.0
1177	        SumMX, SumMY, SumMZ = 0.0, 0.0, 0.0
1178	        SumRFX, SumRFY, SumRFZ = 0.0, 0.0, 0.0
1179	        SumRMX, SumRMY, SumRMZ = 0.0, 0.0, 0.0
1180	
1181	        # Get the global force vector and the global fixed end reaction vector
1182	        P = model.P(combo.name)
1183	        FER = model.FER(combo.name)
1184	
1185	        # Step through each node and sum its forces
1186	        for node in model.nodes.values():
1187	
1188	            # Get the node's coordinates
1189	            X = node.X
1190	            Y = node.Y
1191	            Z = node.Z
1192	
1193	            # Get the nodal forces
1194	            FX = P[node.ID*6+0][0] - FER[node.ID*6+0][0]
1195	            FY = P[node.ID*6+1][0] - FER[node.ID*6+1][0]
1196	            FZ = P[node.ID*6+2][0] - FER[node.ID*6+2][0]
1197	            MX = P[node.ID*6+3][0] - FER[node.ID*6+3][0]
1198	            MY = P[node.ID*6+4][0] - FER[node.ID*6+4][0]
1199	            MZ = P[node.ID*6+5][0] - FER[node.ID*6+5][0]
1200	
1201	            # Get the nodal reactions
1202	            RFX = node.RxnFX[combo.name]
1203	            RFY = node.RxnFY[combo.name]
1204	            RFZ = node.RxnFZ[combo.name]
1205	            RMX = node.RxnMX[combo.name]
1206	            RMY = node.RxnMY[combo.name]
1207	            RMZ = node.RxnMZ[combo.name]
1208	
1209	            # Sum the global forces
1210	            SumFX += FX
1211	            SumFY += FY
1212	            SumFZ += FZ
1213	            SumMX += MX - FY*Z + FZ*Y
1214	            SumMY += MY + FX*Z - FZ*X
1215	            SumMZ += MZ - FX*Y + FY*X
1216	
1217	            # Sum the global reactions
1218	            SumRFX += RFX
1219	            SumRFY += RFY
1220	            SumRFZ += RFZ
1221	            SumRMX += RMX - RFY*Z + RFZ*Y
1222	            SumRMY += RMY + RFX*Z - RFZ*X
1223	            SumRMZ += RMZ - RFX*Y + RFY*X
1224	
1225	        # Add the results to the table
1226	        statics_table.add_row([combo.name, '{:.3g}'.format(SumFX), '{:.3g}'.format(SumRFX),
1227	                                            '{:.3g}'.format(SumFY), '{:.3g}'.format(SumRFY),
1228	                                            '{:.3g}'.format(SumFZ), '{:.3g}'.format(SumRFZ),
1229	                                            '{:.3g}'.format(SumMX), '{:.3g}'.format(SumRMX),
1230	                                            '{:.3g}'.format(SumMY), '{:.3g}'.format(SumRMY),
1231	                                            '{:.3g}'.format(SumMZ), '{:.3g}'.format(SumRMZ)])
1232	
1233	    # Print the static check table
1234	    print(statics_table)
1235	    print('')

1334	def _partition(model: FEModel3D, unp_matrix: NDArray[float64] | lil_matrix, D1_indices: List[int], D2_indices: List[int]) -> Tuple[NDArray[float64], NDArray[float64]] | Tuple[NDArray[float64], NDArray[float64], NDArray[float64], NDArray[float64]]:
1335	    """Partitions a matrix (or vector) into submatrices (or subvectors) based on degree of freedom boundary conditions.
1336	
1337	    :param unp_matrix: The unpartitioned matrix (or vector) to be partitioned.
1338	    :type unp_matrix: ndarray or lil_matrix
1339	    :param D1_indices: A list of the indices for degrees of freedom that have unknown displacements.
1340	    :type D1_indices: list
1341	    :param D2_indices: A list of the indices for degrees of freedom that have known displacements.
1342	    :type D2_indices: list
1343	    :return: Partitioned submatrices (or subvectors) based on degree of freedom boundary conditions.
1344	    :rtype: array, array, array, array
1345	    """
1346	
1347	    # Convert sparse matrices to CSR so they support efficient slicing
1348	    if hasattr(unp_matrix, 'tocsr'):
1349	        unp_matrix = unp_matrix.tocsr()
1350	
1351	    # Determine if this is a 1D vector or a 2D matrix
1352	
1353	    # 1D vectors
1354	    if unp_matrix.shape[1] == 1:
1355	        # Partition the vector into 2 subvectors
1356	        m1 = unp_matrix[D1_indices, :]
1357	        m2 = unp_matrix[D2_indices, :]
1358	        return m1, m2
1359	    # 2D matrices
1360	    else:
1361	        # Partition the matrix into 4 submatrices
1362	        m11 = unp_matrix[D1_indices, :][:, D1_indices]
1363	        m12 = unp_matrix[D1_indices, :][:, D2_indices]
1364	        m21 = unp_matrix[D2_indices, :][:, D1_indices]
1365	        m22 = unp_matrix[D2_indices, :][:, D2_indices]
1366	        return m11, m12, m21, m22

443	        # Get the properties needed to form the local mass matrix
444	        L = self.L()
445	        m = zeros((12, 12))
446	
447	        # Distribute half mass to each node's translational DOFs
448	        # TODO: Distribute the mass based on distance from each load instead
449	        i_node_mass = load_mass*(1 - x)/L
450	        j_node_mass = load_mass*x/L
451	        m[0, 0] = i_node_mass   # FX i-node
452	        m[1, 1] = i_node_mass   # FY i-node
453	        m[2, 2] = i_node_mass   # FZ i-node
454	        m[6, 6] = j_node_mass   # FX j-node
455	        m[7, 7] = j_node_mass   # FY j-node
456	        m[8, 8] = j_node_mass   # FZ j-node
457	
458	        # Add rotational inertia for the mass
459	        # Calculate the rotational inertia: I = m*x²
460	        i_node_rot_inertia = i_node_mass*x**2
461	        j_node_rot_inertia = j_node_mass*(L - x)**2
462	
463	        # Apply rotational inertia about the major and minor axes
464	        # There is no rotational inertia about the torsional axis (zero lever arm)
465	        # Any numerical instability from zeros in the torsional direction will be fixed by the global solver
466	        m[4, 4] = i_node_rot_inertia    # RZ i-node
467	        m[5, 5] = i_node_rot_inertia    # RZ i-node
468	
469	        m[10, 10] = j_node_rot_inertia    # RZ j-node
470	        m[11, 11] = j_node_rot_inertia  # RZ j-node
471	
472	        return m
